```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sinnollareddy_2026_epcoritamab"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-026-01661-1>

Epcoritamab is a subcutaneous CD3xCD20 bispecific IgG1 antibody. Sinnollareddy
et al. used data from the EPCORE NHL-1 (NCT03625037) and EPCORE NHL-3
(NCT04542824) trials to support the approved dosing regimen in relapsed or
refractory follicular lymphoma (R/R FL): a 48 mg full dose given weekly in
cycles 1-3, every 2 weeks in cycles 4-9 and every 4 weeks from cycle 10, after a
3-step step-up schedule (0.16/0.8/3 mg) that replaced the earlier 2-step
schedule (0.16/0.8 mg). The paper contributes two kinds of model:

1. An **updated population PK model** (`Sinnollareddy_2026_epcoritamab`): the
   two-compartment quasi-steady-state (QSS) TMDD model of Li 2025
   (`Li_2025_epcoritamab`) re-estimated with expansion and optimization data
   and extended with body mass index on ka, tumour size on kint and indolent
   NHL subtype on kint (supplementary Table S2).
2. **Logistic exposure-response regressions**, each fitted separately: Emax
   logistic models for objective and complete response (Figure 2), linear
   logistic models for maintained response during Q2W/Q4W dosing (Figure S4),
   for key safety events in all B-NHL patients (Figure 3, Figure S5) and in
   R/R FL (Figure S6), and for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) under the 3-step
   regimen against Cycle 1 AUC (Figure S8) and per-dose Cmax (Figure S9,
   Figure 5B). The paper prints none of the regression coefficients; they were
   digitised by the maintainers from the fitted (red) curves of each panel.
   Each regression is packaged as its own model,
   `Sinnollareddy_2026_epcoritamab_<endpoint>`.

# Population

The PK analysis included 466 adults with R/R B cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma on the
2-step regimen (EPCORE NHL-1 escalation and expansion, EPCORE NHL-3): 186
(39.9%) with indolent NHL (158 with FL), 223 (47.9%) with large B cell lymphoma
and 57 (12.2%) with mantle cell lymphoma; 424 received the 48 mg full dose. The
81 FL patients of the EPCORE NHL-1 optimization cohort received the 3-step
regimen. Supplementary Table S1 gives the cohort demographics: median age 63-71
years (range 20-90), median weight 55.5-77.5 kg (range 39-172; the Japanese
EPCORE NHL-3 cohort is lightest), median BMI 22.4-26.4 kg/m^2 and median tumour
size (SUMPPD) 20.7-37.9 cm^2. Exposure-efficacy analyses used the 160 FL
patients of the escalation and expansion cohorts; exposure-safety analyses used
all 485 B-NHL patients and the FL subset; the 3-step CRS analyses used the 81
optimization-cohort patients.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sinnollareddy_2026_epcoritamab"))$population)
```

## Exposure-response models

The coefficients below are read from the packaged model files. Each was
obtained by calibrating the axis ticks of the cited panel, tracing the red
fitted curve column by column, and fitting the logistic form by least squares
on the probability scale (root-mean-square residual 0.06-0.4 percentage points
for the linear logistic panels and 0.6-1.1 for the Emax panels).

```{r er-index}
# Every packaged exposure-response model is listed above, and vice versa.
stopifnot(setequal(
  er_spec$model,
  grep("^Sinnollareddy_2026_epcoritamab_", nlmixr2lib::modeldb$name, value = TRUE)
))

er_coef <- lapply(er_spec$model, function(nm) {
  ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm))
  est <- setNames(ui$iniDf$est, ui$iniDf$name)
  tibble(
    model = nm,
    output = ui$predDf$var,
    covariate = names(ui$covariateData),
    intercept = unname(est["logit_ref"]),
    slope = unname(est[grep("^e_.*_logit$", names(est))][1]),
    e0 = unname(est["logite0"]),
    emax = unname(est["logitemax"]),
    ec50 = unname(exp(est["lec50"]))
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows()
er <- left_join(er_spec, er_coef, by = "model")

er |>
  transmute(
    Model = suffix, Source = figure, Endpoint = endpoint,
    Covariate = covariate, Output = output,
    Coefficients = ifelse(
      is.na(intercept),
      sprintf("E0 %.4g, Emax %.4g, EC50 %.4g", e0, emax, ec50),
      sprintf("intercept %.4g, slope %.4g", intercept, slope)
    ),
    `Events / N` = paste(events, n, sep = " / ")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

`er_prob()` evaluates any of these regressions on a vector of exposures. It
mirrors the `model()` blocks, which share two templates (linear or Emax logit);
the chunk after it confirms that representative packaged models solved with
`rxSolve()` return the same probabilities.

```{r er-prob}
er_prob <- function(row, x) {
  if (is.na(row$intercept)) {
    plogis(row$e0 + (row$emax - row$e0) * x / (row$ec50 + x))
  } else {
    plogis(row$intercept + row$slope * x)
  }
}

solve_static <- function(model_name, cov_name, x) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_along(x), amt = 0, evid = 0L)
  ev[[cov_name]] <- x
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(model_name)), which = "sigma"),
    events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"
  ))
}

check_models <- c("orr", "bnhl_isr", "maintained_q4w", "3step_crs_auc", "3step_crs_dose4")
for (sfx in check_models) {
  row <- er[er$suffix == sfx, ]
  x <- seq(0.1, 10, length.out = 25)
  s <- solve_static(row$model, row$covariate, x)
  # Same parameters on both sides: only floating-point differences remain.
  stopifnot(max(abs(s[[row$output]] - er_prob(row, x))) < 1e-8)
}
```

# Event-count check of the digitised coefficients

A maximum-likelihood logistic fit with an intercept reproduces the observed
number of events: the sum of the fitted probabilities over the patients equals
the event count. Supplementary Table S5 prints the event counts per Cycle 1-3
Cavg quartile for every safety endpoint (121-122 B-NHL or 40 FL patients per
quartile). Evaluating each digitised curve at the centre of each quartile
(read from the black squares of the figures: 0.8, 3.4, 5.5 and 8.9 ug/mL for
B-NHL; 1.6, 4.1, 5.6 and 8.8 ug/mL for FL) and weighting by the quartile sizes
recovers the printed totals, which checks the digitised intercepts and slopes
together. The two Emax panels of Figure 2 are checked the same way against the
134 responders and 101 complete responders.

```{r score-check}
table_s5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~suffix, ~q1, ~q2, ~q3, ~q4,
  "bnhl_teae_grade3", 100, 87, 81, 89,
  "bnhl_sae", 87, 73, 81, 74,
  "bnhl_discontinuation", 20, 17, 15, 24,
  "bnhl_dose_delay", 59, 69, 64, 58,
  "bnhl_neutropenia_grade3", 24, 34, 31, 46,
  "bnhl_neutropenia", 29, 39, 37, 53,
  "bnhl_infection_grade3", 41, 41, 37, 41,
  "bnhl_infection", 73, 80, 82, 82,
  "bnhl_isr", 38, 52, 64, 74,
  "bnhl_crs", 74, 81, 81, 81,
  "bnhl_crs_grade2", 47, 36, 27, 23,
  "bnhl_crs_tocilizumab", 39, 37, 24, 18,
  "bnhl_icans", 8, 5, 6, 4,
  "fl_teae_grade3", 30, 25, 27, 30,
  "fl_sae", 29, 26, 28, 23,
  "fl_discontinuation", 5, 6, 7, 10,
  "fl_dose_delay", 27, 27, 22, 17,
  "fl_neutropenia_grade3", 7, 10, 11, 11,
  "fl_neutropenia", 8, 11, 14, 13,
  "fl_infection_grade3", 19, 13, 14, 12,
  "fl_infection", 31, 33, 31, 26,
  "fl_isr", 19, 23, 27, 26,
  "fl_crs", 27, 31, 27, 27,
  "fl_crs_grade2", 17, 11, 10, 5,
  "fl_crs_tocilizumab", 11, 8, 12, 8,
  "fl_icans", 4, 0, 3, 1
)
x_bnhl <- c(0.8, 3.4, 5.5, 8.9)
x_fl <- c(1.6, 4.1, 5.6, 8.8)

score <- er |>
  filter(suffix %in% c(table_s5$suffix, "orr", "cr"))
score$predicted <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(score)), function(i) {
  row <- score[i, ]
  x <- if (startsWith(row$suffix, "bnhl")) x_bnhl else x_fl
  sum(row$n / 4 * er_prob(row, x))
}, numeric(1))
score <- mutate(score, pct_diff = 100 * (predicted / events - 1))

score |>
  transmute(Model = suffix, Endpoint = endpoint, `Printed events` = events,
            `Predicted events` = round(predicted, 1),
            `Difference (%)` = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Common-event endpoints land within a few percent; the rarest (ICANS, 8 and
# 23 events) carry a larger discretisation error from the quartile centres.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(score$pct_diff)) < 2,
  all(abs(score$pct_diff[score$events >= 25]) < 5)
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. Two FL cohorts of 150 patients each are
drawn to resemble the EPCORE NHL-1 expansion and optimization cohorts
(supplementary Table S1): age around a median of 64 years (range 20-90),
weight around a median of 75 kg (39-172), height-derived BMI (median about 26
kg/m^2), log-normal SUMPPD around 30 cm^2 (1.5-330) and `TUMTP_INHL = 1`. One
cohort receives the 2-step regimen (0.16/0.8 mg, then 48 mg) and the other the
3-step regimen (0.16/0.8/3 mg, then 48 mg); both then follow 48 mg QW to the
end of cycle 3, Q2W in cycles 4-9 and Q4W from cycle 10 (28-day cycles).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20260101)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260101)
n_arm <- 150

draw_cov <- function(n, id0) {
  wt <- pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(75), 0.2)), 39), 172)
  ht <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 1.70, 0.09), 1.45), 1.98)
  tibble(
    id = id0 + seq_len(n),
    AGE = pmin(pmax(round(rnorm(n, 64, 11)), 20), 90),
    WT = wt,
    BMI = wt / ht^2,
    TUMSZ = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(30), 0.9)), 1.5), 330),
    TUMTP_INHL = 1L
  )
}

later <- c(seq(84, 238, by = 14), seq(252, 420, by = 28))
regimens <- list(
  `2-step` = tibble(time = c(0, 7, seq(14, 77, by = 7), later),
                    amt = c(0.16, 0.8, rep(48, 10), rep(48, length(later)))),
  `3-step` = tibble(time = c(0, 7, 14, seq(21, 77, by = 7), later),
                    amt = c(0.16, 0.8, 3, rep(48, 9), rep(48, length(later))))
)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 84, by = 0.25), seq(85, 448, by = 1))))

make_events <- function(cov, doses, regimen) {
  dose_rows <- tidyr::crossing(cov, doses) |> mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs_rows <- tidyr::crossing(cov, tibble(time = obs_times)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    mutate(regimen = regimen) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

cohort <- bind_rows(draw_cov(n_arm, 0L), draw_cov(n_arm, n_arm))
events <- bind_rows(
  make_events(cohort[seq_len(n_arm), ], regimens[["2-step"]], "2-step"),
  make_events(cohort[n_arm + seq_len(n_arm), ], regimens[["3-step"]], "3-step")
)
summary(cohort[, c("AGE", "WT", "BMI", "TUMSZ")])
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Sinnollareddy_2026_epcoritamab")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "regimen",
                       returnType = "data.frame")
```

## Individual PK parameters

Table S3 summarises the empirical-Bayes individual parameters of the FL
patients by regimen as geometric means. The simulated individual parameters
below use the carried-forward Li 2025 random-effect variances. CL/F, Vc/F and
ka, whose geometric means are governed by the typical values and the weight,
age and BMI effects, agree closely. The remaining parameters differ in the
direction expected from empirical-Bayes estimates of poorly informed random
effects (shrinkage and skew), and kint additionally depends on the unprinted
SUMPPD reference (see Assumptions).

```{r ind-params}
ind <- sim |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  distinct(id, regimen, cl, q, vc, vp, ka, rbase_target, kss, kint) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(across(c(cl, q, vc, vp, ka, rbase_target, kss, kint),
                   ~ exp(mean(log(.x)))), .groups = "drop")

table_s3 <- tibble(
  parameter = c("cl", "q", "vc", "vp", "ka", "rbase_target", "kss", "kint"),
  `2-step` = c(0.531, 0.565, 9.1, 14, 0.521, 2.98, 0.256, 0.0161),
  `3-step` = c(0.49, 0.599, 8.98, 9.69, 0.545, 2.44, 0.335, 0.0153)
)
ind_long <- ind |>
  pivot_longer(-regimen, names_to = "parameter", values_to = "simulated") |>
  left_join(pivot_longer(table_s3, -parameter, names_to = "regimen",
                         values_to = "published"),
            by = c("regimen", "parameter")) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = round(100 * (simulated / published - 1), 1))
knitr::kable(ind_long, digits = 4)

stopifnot(all(abs(ind_long$`Difference (%)`[ind_long$parameter %in% c("cl", "vc", "ka")]) < 15))
```

## Figure 4A: predicted concentrations, 2-step versus 3-step

```{r figure-4a, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
# Replicates Figure 4A of Sinnollareddy 2026: median and 90% prediction
# interval of the predicted epcoritamab concentration for the two regimens.
fig4a <- sim |>
  # Log axis: drop the pre-dose zero concentrations at the first record.
  filter(time >= 0.25) |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc),
            Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(fig4a, aes(time / 7, Q50, colour = regimen, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Epcoritamab concentration (ug/mL)",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Replicates Figure 4A of Sinnollareddy 2026") +
  theme_bw()
```

The 3-step regimen lowers the trough after the intermediate dose and the
concentrations converge once the 48 mg doses accumulate, as in Figure 4A
(median peak about 10 ug/mL at week 12, median Q4W trough about 1-1.5 ug/mL).

# PKNCA: exposure metrics used by the exposure-response models

All exposure metrics used as regressors are computed per subject with PKNCA:
the Cycle 1-3 average concentration (AUC over days 0-84 divided by 84 days),
the Cycle 1 AUC of the 3-step regimen (days 0-35, through the Cycle 2 Day 1
interval), the Cmax of each Cycle 1 dosing interval of the 3-step regimen, and
the steady-state troughs at the end of the Q2W (day 238-252) and Q4W (day
420-448) periods.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
doses <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | regimen + id)
intervals <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(start = 0, end = 84, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE),
  data.frame(start = 0, end = 35, auclast = TRUE),
  data.frame(start = c(0, 7, 14, 21, 28), end = c(7, 14, 21, 28, 35), cmax = TRUE),
  data.frame(start = c(238, 420), end = c(252, 448), cmin = TRUE)
) |>
  # PKNCA needs FALSE, not NA, for the parameters an interval does not request.
  mutate(across(c(auclast, cmax, cmin), ~ dplyr::coalesce(.x, FALSE)))
nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)

metrics <- nca_res |>
  mutate(metric = case_when(
    PPTESTCD == "auclast" & end == 84 ~ "CAV",
    PPTESTCD == "auclast" & end == 35 ~ "AUC_EPCORITAMAB",
    PPTESTCD == "cmax" & end == 7 ~ "CMAX_D1",
    PPTESTCD == "cmax" & end == 14 ~ "CMAX_D2",
    PPTESTCD == "cmax" & end == 21 ~ "CMAX_D3",
    PPTESTCD == "cmax" & end == 28 ~ "CMAX_D4",
    PPTESTCD == "cmax" & end == 35 ~ "CMAX_D5",
    PPTESTCD == "cmin" & end == 252 ~ "CTROUGH_Q2W",
    PPTESTCD == "cmin" & end == 448 ~ "CTROUGH_Q4W",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) |>
  filter(!is.na(metric)) |>
  mutate(value = ifelse(metric == "CAV", PPORRES / 84, PPORRES)) |>
  select(id, regimen, metric, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = value)

summary_tab <- metrics |>
  pivot_longer(-c(id, regimen), names_to = "metric") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  group_by(regimen, metric) |>
  summarise(Q25 = quantile(value, 0.25), Median = median(value),
            Q75 = quantile(value, 0.75), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(summary_tab, digits = 3)
```

The simulated exposure distributions are compared with the distributions the
paper reports for the corresponding regressor: the FL Cycle 1-3 Cavg quartile
bounds of Table S5 (3.44, 4.95 and 6.92 ug/mL; the lowest quartile also holds
the 11 patients on full doses below 48 mg, which the 48 mg-only virtual cohort
lacks), the quartile bounds of the Figure 5B / S9 dose-4 Cmax (about 1.35, 2.2
and 3.25 ug/mL) and Figure S8 Cycle 1 AUC (about 30, 45 and 56 day*ug/mL),
both read from the dashed lines of the figures, and the medians of the
Figure S4 Q2W and Q4W trough box plots (about 4.3 and 1.4 ug/mL, read from the
figure).

```{r exposure-compare}
cmp <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~metric, ~published_median, ~source,
  "2-step", "CAV", 4.95, "Table S5 (FL Q2/Q3 bound)",
  "3-step", "CMAX_D4", 2.2, "Figure 5B dashed lines",
  "3-step", "AUC_EPCORITAMAB", 45, "Figure S8 dashed lines",
  "2-step", "CTROUGH_Q2W", 4.3, "Figure S4 box plot",
  "2-step", "CTROUGH_Q4W", 1.4, "Figure S4 box plot"
) |>
  left_join(summary_tab, by = c("regimen", "metric")) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = round(100 * (Median / published_median - 1), 1))
knitr::kable(cmp, digits = 3)

# A mis-transcribed clearance, volume or dose unit moves these medians by tens
# of percent; the covariate distributions are only approximated, so the
# envelope is generous.
stopifnot(all(abs(cmp$`Difference (%)`) < 35))
```

The 2-step Cycle 1-3 Cavg and the Q2W/Q4W troughs run 7-16% above the
published values, as expected for a virtual cohort that receives every
planned 48 mg dose: the source regressors come from actual dosing histories
with a relative dose intensity of about 90% (Table S6) and include patients on
lower full doses. The early 3-step metrics (dose-4 Cmax and Cycle 1 AUC) run
about 20% below the values read from the figure gridlines; these early
exposures are the most sensitive to the target-mediated terms, including the
unprinted SUMPPD reference, and to the approximated covariate distributions.

# Exposure-response figures

## Figure 2: objective and complete response in R/R FL

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.8}
# Replicates Figure 2A and 2B of Sinnollareddy 2026.
grid_cav <- seq(0, 13.3, length.out = 200)
curve_of <- function(sfx, x) {
  row <- er[er$suffix == sfx, ]
  tibble(suffix = sfx, endpoint = row$endpoint, x = x, p = er_prob(row, x))
}
fig2 <- bind_rows(curve_of("orr", grid_cav), curve_of("cr", grid_cav))
ggplot(fig2, aes(x, p)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Cycle 1-3 Cavg (ug/mL)", y = "Probability",
       title = "Replicates Figure 2A-B of Sinnollareddy 2026") +
  theme_bw()
```

Combining the PK and exposure-response layers, the simulated 48 mg FL cohort
gives the response probabilities below; the observed rates in the pooled
exposure-efficacy population, which included 11 patients on lower full doses,
were 83.8% (objective) and 63.1% (complete).

```{r pk-to-response}
fl_2step <- filter(metrics, regimen == "2-step")
tibble(
  Endpoint = c("Objective response", "Complete response"),
  `Simulated mean probability (%)` = round(100 * c(
    mean(er_prob(er[er$suffix == "orr", ], fl_2step$CAV)),
    mean(er_prob(er[er$suffix == "cr", ], fl_2step$CAV))
  ), 1),
  `Observed (%)` = c(83.8, 63.1)
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Figure 3, Figure S5 and Figure S6: exposure-safety

The open squares are the observed quartile fractions of supplementary Table S5,
plotted at the quartile centres used in the event-count check.

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}
# Replicates Figure 3 and supplementary Figures S5 and S6 of Sinnollareddy 2026.
safety <- er |> filter(grepl("^(bnhl|fl)_", suffix))
grid_safety <- seq(0, 14.5, length.out = 150)
curves <- bind_rows(lapply(safety$suffix, curve_of, x = grid_safety)) |>
  mutate(population = ifelse(startsWith(suffix, "bnhl"), "All B-NHL", "R/R FL"),
         panel = endpoint)
obs <- table_s5 |>
  pivot_longer(q1:q4, names_to = "quartile", values_to = "events_q") |>
  left_join(select(er, suffix, n, endpoint), by = "suffix") |>
  mutate(
    population = ifelse(startsWith(suffix, "bnhl"), "All B-NHL", "R/R FL"),
    q = as.integer(sub("q", "", quartile)),
    x = ifelse(population == "All B-NHL", x_bnhl[q], x_fl[q]),
    p = events_q / (n / 4),
    panel = endpoint
  )
ggplot(curves, aes(x, p, colour = population)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = obs, shape = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 4) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Cycle 1-3 Cavg (ug/mL)", y = "Probability of event", colour = NULL,
       title = "Replicates Figure 3, S5 and S6 of Sinnollareddy 2026") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Figure S8, Figure S9 and Figure 5B: CRS under the 3-step regimen

```{r figure-crs, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates supplementary Figures S8 and S9 and Figure 5B of Sinnollareddy 2026.
x_max <- c(dose1 = 0.0136, dose2 = 0.108, dose3 = 0.305, dose4 = 5.34, dose5 = 10.6)
crs <- bind_rows(
  lapply(c("3step_crs_auc", "3step_crs_grade2_auc", "3step_crs_tocilizumab_auc"),
         curve_of, x = seq(0, 148, length.out = 100)),
  lapply(names(x_max), function(d) {
    sfx <- intersect(c(paste0("3step_crs_", d), paste0("3step_crs_grade2_", d)), er$suffix)
    bind_rows(lapply(sfx, curve_of, x = seq(0, x_max[[d]], length.out = 100)))
  })
) |>
  mutate(
    grade = case_when(grepl("grade2", suffix) ~ "Grade >=2 CRS",
                      grepl("tocilizumab", suffix) ~ "CRS with tocilizumab",
                      TRUE ~ "Any grade CRS"),
    exposure = ifelse(grepl("auc", suffix), "Cycle 1 AUC (day*ug/mL)",
                      paste("Cmax,", sub(".*_(dose[0-9])$", "\\1", suffix), "(ug/mL)"))
  )
ggplot(crs, aes(x, p, colour = grade)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~exposure, scales = "free_x") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Exposure", y = "Probability of event", colour = NULL,
       title = "Replicates Figures S8, S9 and 5B of Sinnollareddy 2026") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Exposure-response coefficients are digitised.** The paper prints no
  intercepts, slopes, E0, Emax or EC50. Every coefficient was digitised by the
  maintainers from the fitted curve of the cited panel (Figures 2, 3 and 5B
  from the article figures; Figures S4, S5, S6, S8 and S9 from the images
  embedded in the supplement) and rounded to four significant figures. The
  event-count check above confirms the digitised curves against the
  independently printed event counts of Table S5. The printed p-values are not
  reproducible from the curves alone and are recorded in the model
  descriptions only.
* **Regressions with no events are not packaged.** Figure 5B also shows
  grade >= 2 CRS after dose 2 (0 of 81) and dose 5 (0 of 80); a logistic
  regression with no events has no finite maximum-likelihood estimate, so these
  two flat panels have no model. Thrombocytopenia and anaemia (Table S5) and
  the duration of response, progression-free and overall survival Kaplan-Meier
  analyses (Figure 2C-E) were not modelled in the paper.
* **The Emax form of Figure 2 follows main-text Eq. 1** with E0 and Emax on
  the logit scale. The printed left-hand side, `log p(x) / (1 - p(x))`, is read
  as the logit `log(p / (1 - p))`.
* **PK random effects are carried from Li 2025.** The update reports fixed
  effects and residual error only (Table S2). The between-subject variances,
  the random effect on the residual-error magnitude and the residual-error
  structure are taken from the Li 2025 parent model
  (`Li_2025_epcoritamab`), which the update re-estimated without stated
  structural changes.
* **Covariate references.** Weight (75 kg) and age (65 years) references are
  those of the Li 2025 parent model. The update does not print the references
  for the two new continuous covariates; BMI is centred at 25 kg/m^2 and
  SUMPPD at 30 cm^2, rounded values near the cohort medians of Table S1
  (BMI 25.6-26.4 kg/m^2 in the EPCORE NHL-1 cohorts; SUMPPD 26.4-37.9 cm^2,
  log-scale median 3.48 = 32.5 cm^2 in the expansion cohort). The BMI choice
  reproduces the Table S3 geometric-mean ka; the simulated kint is lower than
  the Table S3 empirical-Bayes geometric mean, which would favour a smaller
  SUMPPD reference, but empirical-Bayes means of a poorly informed parameter
  are not a reliable centring target, so the rounded median is kept. At the 48
  mg full dose the target is saturated and kint has little effect on exposure
  (main text: the new covariates "had no apparent effect on exposure").
* **Indolent-NHL effect on kint is a ratio.** Table S2 prints "iNHL subtype
  effect on kint = 0.484" without the functional form. It is read as a
  multiplicative ratio (kint x 0.484 for indolent NHL); the alternatives
  (1 + 0.484, or the reciprocal) give follicular lymphoma kint values two to
  three times the Table 1 and Table S3 geometric means for any plausible
  SUMPPD reference.
* **SUMPPD units** are cm^2, as printed in Table S1, rather than the mm^2
  suggested for sum-of-products constructs in the covariate register.
* **Exposure regressors are simulated, not observed.** The source regressors
  are individual predictions from each patient's actual dosing history,
  including interruptions and lower full doses; the virtual cohort here
  receives every planned dose. Cycle 1-3 Cavg is computed over days 0-84.
* **Placeholder residual error.** The logistic models are Bernoulli; the
  `addSd_<output> = fixed(0.001)` term exists only because rxode2 needs an
  observation declaration.
* No erratum for the article was found in Europe PMC (checked 2026-11-17).
